items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: He was helping Bobby along, and he made arrangements for this band.

ctx.x: And for a fast resume, he worked at the Theatrical Club, as I say, and it might be a little bit comical, but Bobby was a stickler and he had started to play trumpet, as I say, only a short time previous. He was wearing tails and white tie, with his little -- let's see, a five-piece jazz band. They used no base. Every once in awhile, somebody would come charging through the club with a base over their shoulder to help out. But in that band was Brad Gowens, and I was going to do some more research on somebody else.…
Bobby a lot of things that he didn't know about players and so on and so forth. He was helping Bobby along, and he made arrangements for this band.

And that's -- primarily to get to the point, that's how I met Bobby Hackett. And it wasn't long before the word got out all over the country about this little cornet player down in Boston that sounded so much like Bix, and that's before Bix's big image across the country was on a few elite privileged people who knew about Bix, and his playing and had the records.
